concepts: SO2 as reducing agent decolourising KMnO4
questions.question: Which gas decolourises potassium permanganate (KMnO4) solution?
questions.solution: (a) Sulphur dioxide. SO2 is a reducing agent and decolourises acidified KMnO4.

questions.question: Which formula represents a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.solution: (b) C5H12. A saturated hydrocarbon has the general formula CnH2n+2.

concepts: reactivity series and reduction of oxides
questions.question: The metal whose oxide can be reduced by common reducing agents:
questions.solution: (a) Copper. The oxides of the other metals are very stable and cannot be reduced by common reducing agents.

questions.question: An organic compound has a vapour density of 22. The molecular formula of the organic compound is: [Atomic weight: C = 12, H = 1]
questions.solution: (d) C3H8. Molecular weight = 2 x 22 = 44; C3H8 = 36 + 8 = 44.

questions.question: In the reaction given below sulphuric acid acts as a/an: S + 2H2SO4 -> 3SO2 + 2H2O
questions.solution: (c) Oxidising agent. Concentrated H2SO4 oxidises S to SO2.

concepts: trend of metallic character down group
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The tendency of losing electrons increases down the Group.
Reason (R): The most reactive metal is placed at the top of Group 1.

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: (c) (A) is true but (R) is false. The most reactive metal of Group 1 is at the bottom of the group.

questions.question: The ore that can be concentrated by using magnetic separation:
questions.solution: (b) Haematite. It is an ore of iron and is magnetic.

questions.question: The diagram shows the bonding in the covalent molecule AB2 (a central atom A bonded to two B atoms, each by a shared pair of electrons). Which option represents the correct electronic configuration of atoms A and B before combining together to form the above molecule?
questions.solution: (d) A = 2, 6; B = 2, 8, 7. A needs two electrons and each B needs one electron to complete the octet, so they form AB2 by sharing.
questions.figure_desc: Electron-sharing diagram of AB2: A in the centre sharing one pair with each of two B atoms. The text options are sufficient to answer.

questions.question: Which of the following option has all the compounds which are members of the same homologous series?
questions.solution: (a) CH4, C2H6, C3H8. All follow the general formula CnH2n+2.

concepts: contact process absorption of SO3 in H2SO4 forming oleum
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In the contact process SO3 gas is not directly dissolved in water to obtain sulphuric acid.
Reason (R): Dense fog or misty droplets of sulphuric acid are formed which is difficult to condense.

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.question: Given below are four ions: Cl-, Li+, Al3+, K+. Identify the pair of ions which have the same electronic configuration. [Atomic number: Cl = 17, Li = 3, Al = 13, K = 19]
questions.solution: (c) Cl- & K+. Both are isoelectronic with 18 electrons.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
concepts: preparation of insoluble salt by precipitation
questions.question: Which pair of reactants can be best used to produce lead (II) sulphate?
questions.solution: (c) Sodium sulphate + Lead nitrate. Lead sulphate is insoluble and is best prepared by precipitation from two soluble salt solutions.

questions.topic: Electrolysis of CuSO4 with Cu electrodes
concepts: electrolysis of CuSO4 with copper electrodes (electro-refining)
questions.question: Aqueous copper (II) sulphate is electrolysed using copper electrodes. Which statement about the electrolysis is not correct?

options.a: An oxidation reaction occurs at the positive electrode.
options.b: The current is carried through the electrolyte by ions.
options.d: The number of copper (II) ions in the electrolyte decreases.

questions.solution: (d) The number of copper (II) ions in the electrolyte decreases. Cu2+ ions deposited at the cathode are replenished by Cu - 2e -> Cu2+ at the anode, so their number stays constant.

concepts: atomic radius and reducing power down group
questions.question: X, Y and Z are three metallic atoms in successive order belonging to the same group such that the atomic radius of X is the smallest. Which of the three atoms is the best reducing agent?

options.d: All three have the same reducing power.

questions.solution: (c) Z. It has the biggest atomic radius, loses electrons most easily and is the strongest reducing agent.

questions.question: 40 cm3 of methane (CH4) is reacted with 60 cm3 of oxygen. The equation for the reaction is: CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O. All volumes are measured at room temperature. What is the total volume of the gases remaining at the end of the reaction?
questions.solution: (b) 40 cm3. 60 cm3 O2 reacts with 30 cm3 CH4 giving 30 cm3 CO2; 10 cm3 CH4 is left unreacted; water is liquid at room temperature. Total = 30 + 10 = 40 cm3.

concepts: lab preparation of ammonia from nitride
questions.question:
A student was instructed to prepare and collect ammonia gas in the laboratory using aluminium nitride. The apparatus was set up as shown in the diagram (aluminium nitride in a flask with a thistle funnel through which substance X is added; the gas passes through a vessel Y; the gas delivery tube dips into water). Study the diagram and answer:
(a) Name the substance X added through the thistle funnel by the student.
(b) Write a balanced equation for the reaction between aluminium nitride and substance X.
(c) Identify the substance Y.
(d) State the function of Y.
(e) Why could the student not collect ammonia gas at the end of the experiment?
questions.solution:
(a) Warm water
(b) AlN + 3H2O -> Al(OH)3 + NH3
(c) Y = Calcium oxide (quicklime)
(d) It acts as the drying agent for ammonia gas.
(e) NH3 is highly soluble in water and cannot be collected by the given procedure (over/into water).

marking_points.point: Y is the drying agent for ammonia
Ammonia is highly soluble in water so it cannot be collected over water

questions.figure_desc: Apparatus for preparing ammonia: flask containing aluminium nitride with a thistle funnel for adding X, delivery tube to a drying vessel Y, and the end of the delivery tube dipping into water; labels 'Ammonia gas', 'Aluminium nitride', X, Y, 'Water'.

State the terms for the following:
(a) Undistilled alcohol containing a large amount of methanol.
(b) A salt formed by the partial replacement of the hydroxyl group of a di-acidic or a tri-acidic base by an acid radical.
(c) Organic compounds having the same molecular formula but different structural formula.
(d) The tendency of an atom to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself when combined in a compound.
(e) The type of covalent bond in which electrons are shared unequally between the combining atoms.

Salt formed by partial replacement of the hydroxyl group of a di-acidic or tri-acidic base by an acid radical
Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formula
Tendency of an atom to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself
Covalent bond in which electrons are shared unequally

questions.solution:
(a) Spurious alcohol (or denatured alcohol)
(b) Basic salt
(c) Isomers
(d) Electronegativity
(e) Polar covalent bond

questions.question:
The reaction between concentrated sulphuric acid and magnesium: Mg + 2H2SO4 -> MgSO4 + 2H2O + SO2. If 60 g of magnesium is used, calculate:
(a) The mass of sulphuric acid needed for the reaction.
(b) The volume of sulphur dioxide gas liberated at S.T.P.
[Atomic weight: Mg = 24, H = 1, S = 32, O = 16]
questions.solution:
(a) 24 g Mg reacts with 2 x 98 g H2SO4. 60 g Mg needs 2 x 98 x 60/24 = 490 g H2SO4.
(b) 24 g Mg liberates 22.4 L SO2 at STP. 60 g Mg liberates 22.4 x 60/24 = 56 L SO2.

questions.question:
A gas cylinder can hold 150 g of hydrogen under certain conditions of temperature and pressure. If an identical cylinder with the same capacity can hold 450 g of gas 'G' under the same conditions of temperature and pressure, find:
(a) the vapour density of the gas 'G'.
(b) the molecular weight of gas 'G'.
questions.solution:

(b) Molecular weight = 2 x VD = 2 x 3 = 6.

concepts: empirical and molecular formula from percentage composition
questions.question: An organic compound 'X' contains carbon, oxygen and hydrogen only. The percentage of carbon and hydrogen are 47.4% and 10.5% respectively. The relative molecular mass of 'X' is 76. Find the empirical formula and the molecular formula of 'X'. [Atomic weight: C = 12, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.solution:
O = 100 - (47.4 + 10.5) = 42.1%.
Moles: C 47.4/12 = 3.95; H 10.5/1 = 10.5; O 42.1/16 = 2.63.
Simplest ratio (divide by 2.63): C 1.5 : H 3.99 : O 1; multiply by 2: C 3 : H 8 : O 2.
Empirical formula = C3H8O2; empirical weight = 36 + 8 + 32 = 76.
n = 76/76 = 1, so molecular formula = C3H8O2.

marking_points.point: Simplest whole-number ratio C3 : H8 : O2

questions.question:
Draw the dot and cross structure of the following:
(a) An ionic compound formed when Mg reacts with dilute HCl.
(b) A covalent compound formed when H2 reacts with Cl2.
(c) The positive ion produced when ammonia gas is dissolved in water.

questions.solution:

HCl correct shared pair with Cl lone pairs
NH4+ correct structure with coordinate bond, brackets and +1 charge

concepts: precipitation vs direct combination vs titration
questions.question:
P, Q, R and S are different methods of preparation of salts: P - Simple displacement; Q - Neutralisation by titration; R - Precipitation; S - Direct combination. Choose the most appropriate method to prepare the following salts:
(A) PbCl2
(B) FeCl3
(C) Na2SO4

answer_items.prompt: Method to prepare PbCl2
Method to prepare FeCl3
Method to prepare Na2SO4

questions.solution:
(A) R - Precipitation (2NaCl + Pb(NO3)2 -> PbCl2 + 2NaNO3)
(B) S - Direct combination (2Fe + 3Cl2 -> 2FeCl3)
(C) Q - Neutralisation by titration (2NaOH + H2SO4 -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O)
